title: Trump Tariffs Target 14 Partners as Nasdaq Ends 0.62% Lower
summary: The US proposed Trump tariffs of up to 20% on China, 25% on India and 35% on Vietnam. The Nasdaq closed 0.62% lower after an early drop of more than 4%.
body_markdown:
JPMorgan analysts said "the macro impact from this increase is likely to be modest" and noted that "several key imports are still exempt from tariffs, including tech goods," according to the same Reuters report.


> "The additional tariff burden is likely to be small, but will still provide a marginal boost to prices," said Stephen Brown, chief North America economist at Capital Economics, as reported by Reuters.


Brown added that the extra burden should keep core goods[inflation](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-inflation-affects-investing-risk-types-real-returns/) firm into next year.


## What Does the Section 301 Tariff Proposal Do?


It would add tariffs on goods from 14 economies whose practices USTR found "are unreasonable and burden or restrict U.S. commerce." According to the[USTR release](https://ustr.gov/about/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases/2026/november/ustr-makes-determinations-and-proposes-actions-14-section-301-investigations-relating-structural) , each rate is set net of existing Section 301 tariffs, certain products listed in annexes are exempt, and several rates account for existing or pending trade deals. USTR listed the proposed rates as follows.


Economy Proposed tariff Rate tied to a trade deal


China Up to 20% (up to 10% on Annex A goods) Accounts for the 20% rate in the Kuala Lumpur Joint Arrangement


Vietnam Up to 35% 20% with a reciprocal trade agreement


India Up to 25% 17% with a reciprocal trade agreement


Singapore Up to 20% 10% under consideration with an agreement


Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Cambodia, Bangladesh Up to 18% Accounts for each existing trade agreement


Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland Up to 15% Accounts for each existing deal


European Union 15% Accounts for the US-EU framework agreement


For China, the proposal accounts for the 20% tariff rate announced in the Kuala Lumpur Joint Arrangement that Trump and Xi Jinping reached on Oct. 30, 2025, and exempts products on the US-China Board of Trade lists recommended for reduced tariffs, USTR said.[The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/us/2026/11/25/us-proposes-tariffs-on-trade-partners-including-china-india-and-eu/) reported that the new levy comes on top of the 25% placed on China in Trump's first term and could reach 40% if the truce, which runs until Jan. 10, collapses. Beijing rejected the idea of overcapacity but stopped short of retaliation, and many expect the truce to be extended when Trump and Xi meet at the G20 summit in Miami in December, per the same report.


India and the US agreed a trade deal framework in February, but a final agreement has not been reached, The National reported. Under the proposal, India's rate would be 17% with a deal and up to 25% if talks fail.


Written comments and requests to appear are due Jan. 5, 2027, and USTR will hold hearings on Jan. 25, 2027. Reuters reported that the new rates are unlikely to be imposed until February or March.


US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the action can "level the playing field for American workers," according to USTR's statement.
